title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #9

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which part of the plant holds it firmly in the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Fruit
   B. Roots
   C. Flowers
   D. Leaves

2. Why should you not pull leaves off a young plant for fun? (1 mark)
   A. Leaves are heavy
   B. The plant has too many leaves
   C. The leaves make the roots sweet
   D. The plant needs its leaves to make food

3. Which part of the plant is usually flat, green and spread out to catch light? (1 mark)
   A. Root
   B. Stem
   C. Seed
   D. Leaf

4. Which of these is an invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Earthworm
   C. Frog
   D. Snake

5. Which group of vertebrates feeds its young on milk? (1 mark)
   A. Reptiles
   B. Mammals
   C. Birds
   D. Fish

6. Where does the digestive tube begin? (1 mark)
   A. Small intestine
   B. Mouth
   C. Stomach
   D. Anus

7. Which part of the digestive system is the widest tube near the end? (1 mark)
   A. Large intestine
   B. Small intestine
   C. Gullet
   D. Anus

8. What is diarrhoea? (1 mark)
   A. Food coming out of the mouth
   B. Passing hard dry faeces
   C. A swollen stomach
   D. Passing loose watery faeces many times

9. How often should teeth be brushed? (1 mark)
   A. At least twice a day
   B. Once a month
   C. Never
   D. Once a year

10. What is constipation? (1 mark)
   A. Vomiting
   B. Having worms
   C. Passing watery faeces
   D. Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty

11. What does mass mean? (1 mark)
   A. The space an object takes up
   B. How hot an object is
   C. The amount of matter in an object
   D. How bright an object is

12. What does a football need to keep its shape? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Air
   C. Milk
   D. Sand

13. Steam from a boiling pot is really (1 mark)
   A. A red liquid
   B. A white solid
   C. A block of ice
   D. An invisible gas

14. There are 750 ml of milk in a jug. 300 ml is poured out. How much is left? (1 mark)
   A. 350 ml
   B. 1050 ml
   C. 450 ml
   D. 550 ml

15. Why are solids like bricks and stones used to build houses? (1 mark)
   A. They keep their shape and can support weight
   B. They are invisible
   C. They spread out
   D. They flow easily

16. Which unit is used for the mass of a sack of maize? (1 mark)
   A. Litre
   B. Metre
   C. Kilogram
   D. Second

17. Which grouping of gases is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Air, steam and cooking gas are gases
   B. Sugar, oil and air are solids
   C. Stone, water and wood are liquids
   D. Milk, chalk and steam are solids

18. In a school, who could check that bins are emptied and clean? (1 mark)
   A. Only the wind
   B. Only the visitors
   C. Class monitors
   D. Nobody

19. Which waste can be reused as a pencil holder? (1 mark)
   A. Old leaves
   B. An empty tin
   C. Banana peel
   D. Egg shells

20. What should you do if you find a needle or broken glass in waste? (1 mark)
   A. Play with it
   B. Tell a teacher and do not touch it
   C. Pick it up with bare hands
   D. Put it in your pocket

21. Which disease can spread by mosquitoes breeding in old tins that hold water? (1 mark)
   A. Sunburn
   B. Malaria
   C. Toothache
   D. Diarrhoea only

22. Which is the best way to manage the food remains from the school kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Put them in a compost pit
   B. Throw them in a river
   C. Bury plastic with them
   D. Burn them near classrooms

23. What is the best way to deal with metal scrap in a school? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it in a river
   B. Sell it to a scrap dealer or reuse it
   C. Burn it
   D. Bury it in the school garden

24. A cyclist presses the brakes and slows down. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Increases speed
   B. Holds objects together
   C. Decreases speed
   D. Starts motion

25. Which force pulls objects down towards the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. Sound
   B. Gravity
   C. Friction
   D. Wind

26. Why does a mango fall from a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Light pulls it
   B. Gravity pulls it down
   C. Friction pushes it
   D. Sound moves it

27. Which of these will make a block slide the shortest distance on a ramp? (1 mark)
   A. Sandpaper
   B. Oiled plastic
   C. Smooth tile
   D. Glass

28. A rolling ball slowly comes to a stop on the ground mainly because of (1 mark)
   A. Colour
   B. Friction
   C. Light
   D. Sound

29. Why is it better to use daylight than electric light in the day? (1 mark)
   A. It makes rooms dark
   B. It saves money
   C. It is unsafe
   D. It costs more

30. Which of these is NOT a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. An electric bulb
   B. A torch
   C. A mirror
   D. A candle

31. Why do some farmers use bright lights near animal pens at night? (1 mark)
   A. To warm animals
   B. To scare away wild animals
   C. To make animals sleepy
   D. To make animals heavier

32. What does light help us to do? (1 mark)
   A. Taste
   B. Smell
   C. Hear
   D. See

33. How can lights help protect a home? (1 mark)
   A. Lights make walls hot
   B. Lights make doors open
   C. Security lights help keep thieves away
   D. Lights make people sleep

34. Which of these is NOT a source of heat? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. A burning log
   C. A cold stone in the shade
   D. A kettle

35. Which of these is a source of heat from burning? (1 mark)
   A. A cup
   B. Charcoal
   C. A book
   D. A ruler

36. Which use of heat helps us on a cold morning? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping us warm
   B. Making things dark
   C. Growing shadows
   D. Making sound

37. Why does an ice cube melt in your hand? (1 mark)
   A. The ice makes heat
   B. The hand makes water
   C. Cold goes into your hand
   D. Heat goes from your hand into the ice

38. How does heat help plants and animals? (1 mark)
   A. It stops growth
   B. It makes them sleepy
   C. It keeps them warm enough to live
   D. It makes them cold

39. Why do wet clothes dry faster in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. The sun makes water colder
   B. The sun makes them heavy
   C. The heat evaporates the water
   D. The sun adds water

40. Which of these is unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Switching off an iron
   B. Asking an adult to light a fire
   C. Playing with matches
   D. Using gloves

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain why a mirror or a shiny cup is not a source of light. (3 marks)

42. Describe how you can care for plants at school and at home. Give five ways. (5 marks)

43. A shopkeeper has 2 kg of sugar and 750 g of salt. Find the total mass in grams. (3 marks)

44. Why is used washing water not safe for drinking? Give one good way to use it. (3 marks)

45. Explain how wasting water can affect other people and the family. (4 marks)

46. Explain the importance of heat in daily life. (5 marks)

47. Write three safety rules when observing animals in the school compound. (3 marks)

48. Give two examples each of transparent and opaque materials. (2 marks)

49. Describe what happens in the small intestine and why it is important. (4 marks)

50. Explain why we should care for animals and describe how it can be done at home and at school. (5 marks)

51. A block is pulled along a rough floor and along a smooth floor with the same force. Describe and explain what you would see. (4 marks)

52. A jug has 1 litre of juice. 350 ml is poured into a cup. How much is left in the jug? (3 marks)

53. Describe how windows, roofs and walls can be used to make a house brighter by day. (4 marks)

54. Give three ways of caring for animals. (3 marks)

55. Give four healthy eating habits that keep the digestive system healthy. (4 marks)

56. Give three ways of protecting water sources. (3 marks)

57. Name two ways of lighting a house during the day. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Roots
   Roots anchor the plant in the ground.

2. D — The plant needs its leaves to make food
   Leaves are the food factories of the plant.

3. D — Leaf
   The flat, green shape of a leaf helps it catch light.

4. B — Earthworm
   An earthworm has a soft body and no backbone.

5. B — Mammals
   Mammals feed their babies with milk.

6. B — Mouth
   Food enters the body through the mouth.

7. A — Large intestine
   The large intestine is wider than the small intestine.

8. D — Passing loose watery faeces many times
   Diarrhoea means loose watery faeces.

9. A — At least twice a day
   Brushing morning and night keeps teeth healthy.

10. D — Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty
   Constipation means hard faeces that are difficult to pass.

11. C — The amount of matter in an object
   Mass is the amount of matter in something.

12. B — Air
   The air inside fills the football.

13. D — An invisible gas
   Steam is water as a gas and is invisible. The cloud we see is tiny water drops.

14. C — 450 ml
   750 - 300 = 450 ml.

15. A — They keep their shape and can support weight
   Solids keep their shape.

16. C — Kilogram
   Mass is measured in grams and kilograms.

17. A — Air, steam and cooking gas are gases
   Air, steam and cooking gas are gases.

18. C — Class monitors
   Monitors can share the responsibility.

19. B — An empty tin
   A clean tin can be reused.

20. B — Tell a teacher and do not touch it
   Sharp objects should be handled by adults using tools.

21. B — Malaria
   Mosquitoes spread malaria and breed in standing water.

22. A — Put them in a compost pit
   Kitchen waste can be composted.

23. B — Sell it to a scrap dealer or reuse it
   Metal can be recycled.

24. C — Decreases speed
   Brakes use friction to slow the bicycle.

25. B — Gravity
   Gravity pulls things towards the centre of the Earth.

26. B — Gravity pulls it down
   Gravity acts on every object.

27. A — Sandpaper
   Rough surfaces have the most friction.

28. B — Friction
   Friction between the ball and the ground slows it.

29. B — It saves money
   Sunlight is free.

30. C — A mirror
   A mirror only reflects light.

31. B — To scare away wild animals
   Bright lights can scare away predators.

32. D — See
   Light lets us see objects.

33. C — Security lights help keep thieves away
   Thieves avoid places where they can be seen.

34. C — A cold stone in the shade
   A cold stone gives out no heat of its own.

35. B — Charcoal
   Charcoal gives out heat when it burns.

36. A — Keeping us warm
   Heat keeps our bodies warm.

37. D — Heat goes from your hand into the ice
   Heat moves from the warm hand to the ice.

38. C — It keeps them warm enough to live
   Life needs suitable warmth.

39. C — The heat evaporates the water
   Heat makes water turn to vapour.

40. C — Playing with matches
   Matches can start fires.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: It does not make its own light. It only reflects light that falls on it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for not making light, 1 mark for reflecting, 1 mark for explanation.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Water when dry, weed, do not trample, plant trees, do not pick flowers, put waste in bins, protect from animals (any five).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way up to 5.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2750 g.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 2 kg = 2000 g, 1 mark for adding 750 g and 1 mark for the answer.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has dirt and germs. It can be used to water plants or mop floors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirty water, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for a safe use.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Less water is left for others, especially in dry areas. The family pays more for water and may have to fetch more.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for others and 2 marks for family.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Heat keeps us warm, cooks food, dries clothes and crops, helps plants grow, makes rain by evaporation, and is used to make metals and glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not pick up animals you do not know, do not harm animals, wash hands after touching soil or animals, return animals to where they were found.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Transparent: clear glass, clear plastic, clean water. Opaque: wood, metal, stone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Digestion is finished there. Digested food passes through the wall into the blood. The blood carries it to all parts of the body for energy, growth and repair.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 4.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Animals give us milk, meat, eggs and honey and help us in work. They are part of nature. We give them food, water, shelter and medical care and we do not hurt them. At school we keep the compound safe for birds.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for ways.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: The block moves slower or a shorter distance on the rough floor. Rough floors give more friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: 650 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 1 litre = 1000 ml, 1 mark for the subtraction 1000 - 350 and 1 mark for the answer.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Large windows let in light, translucent roof sheets let in light, light-coloured walls reflect light, open curtains.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give food and clean water, provide shelter, keep their homes clean, treat sick animals, do not beat them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Eat a balanced diet, eat fruits and vegetables, drink clean water, chew slowly, wash fruits, avoid rotten food, cover food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each habit up to 4.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plant trees near rivers, do not throw waste in water, do not wash in springs, keep animals away from drinking sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Windows and translucent roof sheets (skylights).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
